exercise.name: Hindu Push-Up
steps: Start with hips high and arms straight, your body making an upside-down V.
Bend your elbows and swoop your chest down and forward, close to the floor.
Straighten your arms to lift your chest, hips low, looking ahead.
Push your hips back up into the V to finish the rep.
exercise.one_line_summary: Two pictures: (1) the upside-down V (hips high, arms straight and in line with the back, heels toward the floor, head between the arms); (2) the arched finish (arms straight under the shoulders, hips low just off the floor, back arched, chest up, looking ahead). Hands and feet stay planted. Chest is the target; front delts and triceps help.

setup.target: Hands about shoulder-width, planted for the whole rep.
setup.why: The movement swoops between two fixed contact points (S1).

setup.target: Feet about hip-to-shoulder width (ankles ~0.40 m apart), on the balls of the feet.
setup.why: Traditional dand stance; feet stay put while the ankles roll (S1).

movement.measure: pelvis rot X (90 = flat face-down); hip joint height
movement.start: 134.6 (pelvis tipped head-down 45 deg), hip joint ~0.83 m
movement.end: 66 (pelvis head-up 24 deg), hip joint ~0.34 m, front of the pelvis ~0.25 m off the floor
movement.path: Library: elbows bend and the chest swoops forward close to the floor, then the arms straighten with the hips low.
movement.tolerance: V hip angle 70-95 deg; end pelvis front 0.10-0.30 m off the floor (hip extension kept under ~20 deg, the rest of the arch is in the spine)

movement.path: Back goes from flat to arched (cobra / up-dog).

movement.measure: arm elevation in the torso frame
movement.end: 35.7 (arms vertical under the shoulders, measured from the spine05->neck chord of the arched trunk)
movement.path: Shoulders travel forward over and past the hands.

movement.measure: elbow bend in the two pictures
movement.path: Bends deeply only in the middle swoop (not pictured).

movement.measure: grip centre and toe tip in the world
movement.path: Hands stay on one spot; the feet roll from the balls (heels toward the floor) onto the toes.

muscles.emg: No EMG study of the Hindu push-up (searched). Push-up (close variant): pectoralis near-maximal relative activation across hand positions (S2). Marcolin 2015: push-up variants load pectoralis major and triceps most; changing the hand base shifts the balance (S3).
muscles.role: Pushes the body up in the press-up phase; library primary.
muscles.surface: Front of the upper chest from the breastbone out to the armpit.

muscles.emg: In push-ups triceps activation was higher than pectoralis in absolute terms (S2).
Not measured; listed among the muscles worked (S1).
muscles.role: Drive the arm forward and hold the V overhead position.
Control the arch and the V.

mistakes.mistake: Hips resting on the floor at the finish
mistakes.what_it_looks_like: Thighs and pelvis flop onto the floor in the arched position.
mistakes.why_it_matters: Library: hips low, not down; the arms and shoulders should hold the body.

mistakes.what_it_looks_like: Elbows bent, head dropped toward the floor in the start.

sources.what_it_gave: Inverted V start, bend elbows and drop the chin, sweep the hips under and the chest/head up with straight arms, push the hips back to the V; muscles: abdominals, pectorals, triceps, deltoids, serratus.

sources.citation: Intziegianni K, Katsamis E, Michaelides M, Parpa K. 2026. Electromyographic activation of the pectoralis major and triceps brachii muscles during standard, diamond, and wide hand position push-ups. Muscles 5(1):18. doi:10.3390/muscles5010018
sources.what_it_gave: Push-ups: pectoralis and triceps near-maximal relative activation; triceps > pectoralis in raw amplitude.

sources.citation: Marcolin G, Petrone N, Moro T, Battaglia G, Bianco A, Paoli A. 2015. Selective activation of shoulder, trunk, and arm muscles: a comparative analysis of different push-up variants. J Athl Train 50(11):1126-1132. doi:10.4085/1062-6050-50.9.09
sources.what_it_gave: 12 muscles across 5 push-up variants: triceps and pectoralis major most active (narrow base highest); abdominal and back muscles act as stabilisers. No study of the Hindu push-up itself exists (searched 12 Nov 2026), so the push-up is the close variant (grade B).

clip_check.check: Start V: arms straight in line with the back, hips high
clip_check.target: elbow 0-10; hip angle 70-95 deg; hip joint > 0.7 m

clip_check.check: End arch: arms straight under the shoulders, hips low but off the floor
clip_check.target: elbow 0-10; arms vertical; pelvis front 0.10-0.30 m above the floor; trunk really leans (needs the 12 Nov animate.py root-key fix)

clip_check.check: Hands planted at the same spot in both pictures
clip_check.target: hand moves < 0.03 m; lowest body point -0.005..+0.005 in both pictures (designed grip centre 0.100 slanted / 0.082 vertical)

clip_check.check: Balls of the feet on the floor in both
clip_check.target: toes -0.005..+0.005 m (designed +0.002: ankle 0.193 at rot 45, 0.218 at rot 70); toe tip moves < 0.03 m

clip_check.check: Overhead armpit skin in the V

clip_check.target: chest strongest red in both pictures (it faces the floor: check it shows from the camera)
